title_de: 53-Man Roster Prediction: Wer schafft es in den finalen Roster?
title_en: 53-man roster prediction: who makes the final cut?
teaser_de: Vor dem Training Camp ein Tipp für den 53er-Kader. Am engsten wird es bei Receivern, Linebackern und Cornerbacks.
teaser_en: A pick for the 53-man roster before training camp. The tightest battles are at receiver, linebacker and cornerback.
body_en:
Today's the day: the 49ers' veterans report to the facility at Levi's Stadium for training camp. On Sunday, the players will be out on the practice field for the first time.

Roster spots are more contested this year than they have been in a long time. Kyle Shanahan's coaching staff has significantly more options, especially in terms of depth, and will have to make several tough decisions on August 30: who makes the 53-man roster?

### Here is my current 53-man roster prediction:

### Offense

### Quarterback (2)

Brock Purdy and Mac Jones have their spots locked up.

Will the 49ers carry two or three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster? That is the big question. Last year, they went into the season with only Brock Purdy and Mac Jones, since Kurtis Rourke spent the season on the NFI list with his torn ACL.

This year, however, Kurtis Rourke is healthy and a serious candidate for the final roster.

Because of the depth at other positions, I decided against Rourke here. If the Canadian has a good preseason, though, he has a very good chance of landing one of the 53 roster spots.

### Running back (4)

Prediction: Christian McCaffrey, Kyle Juszczyk, Jordan James, Kaelon Black

PUP: Isaac Guerendo

All four of the players named above are as good as certain to make the final 53-man roster. Jordan James is probably Christian McCaffrey's first backup, and Kaelon Black is also safe as a third-round pick.

The question here is whether Kyle Shanahan and co. will go into the season with five running backs on the active roster, as in recent years. Because the other position groups are so deep, I went with only four running backs.

But you can expect Patrick Taylor Jr. to land on the practice squad and be elevated for individual games.

A big question mark is Isaac Guerendo. The former fourth-round pick is still rehabbing the torn pectoral muscle he suffered in the offseason. Whether he will be healthy for training camp, or when he will return, is still open. Even without the injury, it is questionable whether Guerendo would make the active 53-man roster.

### Tight end (3)

Prediction: George Kittle, Luke Farrell, Jake Tonges

Will George Kittle be healthy for Week 1, or will he start the season on the PUP list? One thing is certain: if he stays on the PUP list after cut day, he automatically misses at least four games. As of today, I expect us to see George Kittle again early in the season. Whether that will be in time for the game in Australia remains to be seen.

Luke Farrell and Jake Tonges should have their roster spots locked up.

Other contenders for active roster spots are Brayden Willis and undrafted rookie Khalil Dinkins. However, Dinkins, formerly of the Penn State Nittany Lions, was placed on the NFI list last week. As of now, we don't know how serious his injury is, but he can be activated from the NFI list at any time before cut day. If he returns to the practice field soon, his blocking skills could put him in competition with Luke Farrell for a roster spot.

Brayden Willis will probably start the season on the practice squad. He could be elevated for individual games, especially early in the season while George Kittle is not yet ready.

### Wide receiver (6)

Prediction: Mike Evans, Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, Demarcus Robinson

The WR position is as contested as almost no other.

Evans, Pearsall and Stribling should have their places on the 53-man roster locked up. Behind them, everything is wide open. Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, Demarcus Robinson and Christian Kirk are battling for the remaining three roster spots.

Demarcus Robinson probably has the edge here thanks to his experience in the NFL and in the 49ers offense. Unlike most of the others, he can also play every WR position in Kyle Shanahan's offense. Given the injury history of Ricky Pearsall and Mike Evans (plus his age), that makes him very valuable.

Jordan Watkins impressed again and again last offseason. Especially in training camp and in the joint practices against the Broncos, there were repeated positive reports. But in the preseason game against Denver he suffered a high ankle sprain. After his return, he no longer played a role during the season.

Like Demarcus Robinson, Watkins has the ability to play as the X receiver. He also brings speed and explosiveness. If Watkins stays healthy in training camp, I expect him to land on the active 53-man roster.

The last active roster spot in my prediction goes to Jacob Cowing. For him, too: he has to stay healthy. Last year, Kyle Shanahan called him probably the best wide receiver of the offseason (OTAs plus minicamp). In training camp, however, the first of several hamstring injuries followed, which is why he had to watch the entire season from the sidelines. Cowing is the favorite for the punt returner job. If he stays healthy in training camp and continues to impress, he could even play a bigger role in the offense.

That makes Christian Kirk the odd man out, which will probably come as a big surprise to most. I could well imagine Kirk being traded if another team needs reinforcements because of injuries.

The WR position is incredibly contested. Right now, it is very hard to predict what will really happen. The team has definitely learned from last year and has plenty of options.

### Offensive tackle (4)

Prediction: Trent Williams, Colton McKivitz, Vederian Lowe, Enrique Cruz

At tackle, everything is pretty much settled. Trent Williams starts at left tackle, Colton McKivitz is the undisputed starter at right tackle and Vederian Lowe is the swing tackle. Enrique Cruz has potential but still has a lot to learn. It's safe to assume we won't see him on the field in the regular season this year.

With Austen Pleasants, the team also has a very solid option for the practice squad.

### Interior offensive line (6)

Prediction: Jake Brendel, Brett Toth, Dominick Puni, Robert Jones, Connor Colby, Carver Willis

Jake Brendel has his spot as starting center locked up. His backup is Brett Toth, who came over from Philadelphia in the offseason and can be used in multiple spots. The former Eagle is also in the competition for the starting LG spot. Dominick Puni is the undisputed starting right guard.

Besides Toth, Robert Jones, Connor Colby, Carver Willis and Nick Zakelj are also in the race for the left guard spot.

Thanks to his experience in the scheme (with the Dolphins under Mike McDaniel), Robert Jones certainly has a good shot at the starting job. His main competitor is probably Connor Colby, who has already played regular-season games at this position. Carver Willis is probably more of a dark-horse candidate for the starting spot. The rookie from the University of Washington will more likely play a role at guard or center in the future.

Nick Zakelj was already on the practice squad last year, and you can expect the same this year. With his flexibility to play center as well as both guard positions, he is still a valuable part of the team.

### Defense

### Defensive tackle (4)

Prediction: Osa Odighizuwa, Alfred Collins, CJ West, Gracen Halton

All the players named above should have their roster spots locked up. The question here is whether another defensive tackle makes the jump onto the 53-man roster.

One candidate is Sebastian "Hulk" Valdez. Valdez made a number of plays last year, both in the preseason and in practice.

### Defensive end (5)

Prediction: Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Romello Height, Sam Okuayinonu, Keion White

Both Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams are expected back on the practice field during camp and are therefore safe on the 53-man roster. Keion White, who will be back on the field at the start of training camp after his gunshot injury in the offseason, is probably a lock as well. Third-round pick Romello Height is also certain to be on the active roster.

Should the 49ers sign another high-profile free agent at this position (e.g. Joey Bosa, Jadeveon Clowney), things could get a bit tight for Sam Okuayinonu. At the moment, however, that doesn't seem realistic. You can expect Sam O to be on the 49ers' final 53-man roster at the end of August.

### Linebacker (6)

Prediction: Fred Warner, Dre Greenlaw, Nick Martin, Luke Gifford, Jaden Dugger, Tatum Bethune

Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw are the starters and therefore safe. So is Luke Gifford as a core special teamer and possibly also as a starter on defense.

Behind them, the team has an incredible number of options: Nick Martin, Jaden Dugger, Tatum Bethune, Garrett Wallow and Jalen Graham are probably battling for two, maybe three remaining roster spots.

As a third-round pick last year, Nick Martin should have a good chance here. Still, he has to prove in training camp that he can play at this level. If he impresses, he could secure the spot as the starting SAM linebacker. A cut or trade can't be ruled out either, though.

LB coach KJ Wright is a huge fan of rookie linebacker Jaden Dugger. I expect him to bet on Dugger's potential and not want to risk losing him. With his speed, size and explosiveness, Dugger could get playing time on special teams early on in particular.

Tatum Bethune showed last year that he can be relied on as a backup. With good performances in camp and in the preseason, he might even make a case for the starting SAM linebacker job.

That would leave Garrett Wallow off the final 53-man roster, even though he showed impressively last year that he can play at the NFL level. A trade would definitely be conceivable here. Maybe to Robert Saleh in Tennessee?

### Cornerback (4)

Prediction: Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green, Jack Jones, Ephesians Prysock

The competition at cornerback is enormous as well. Deommodore Lenoir is the only safe starter. Behind him, Renardo Green, Jack Jones, Ephesians Prysock, Darrell Luter Jr., Eli Apple and Jakob Robinson are fighting for the second starting job and the remaining roster spots.

Green and Jones are the favorites for the starting job next to Lenoir. This battle will be extremely exciting to watch.

Behind them, fourth-rounder Ephesians Prysock should have his roster spot locked up.

It is rather unlikely that the 49ers will keep anyone else on the roster. One name to definitely keep an eye on over the next few weeks is Jakob Robinson. The former undrafted free agent from BYU is entering his second NFL season and had a strong training camp and solid preseason games last year. After an injury at the end of training camp, however, he was placed on injured reserve.

### Nickel back (3)

Prediction: Upton Stout, Nate Hobbs, Siran Neal

There shouldn't be any surprises here. Stout will probably go into the season as the starter but can't be too sure of himself. Nate Hobbs has already shown in the NFL that he can play the nickel position at a very high level. In recent years, however, he was used more often as an outside corner and couldn't really convince there.

Siran Neal is definitely a lock as a core special teamer.

### Safety (3)

Prediction: Malik Mustapha, Marques Sigle, Ji'Ayir Brown

The safety position is definitely one of the big weak spots on the entire team. Due to a lack of competition, you shouldn't expect any surprises here. Realistic options are Ashtyn Davis and Derrick Canteen.

### Special teams (3)

Prediction: Eddy Pineiro, Corliss Waitman, Jon Weeks

The kicker and long snapper positions are filled. At punter, Corliss Waitman and Jack Bouwmeester are battling it out. With his NFL experience, though, Waitman probably has the better chance at the starting job.
